Eocene lake environments were characterized by a deep water/off-shore zone, a shallow water/near-shore zone, and a transition zone in between, and that each of these zones is characterized by a unique assemblage of fossils, which can be used as a proxy to infer the depth of the lake.
Eocene fish, insect, plant, and coprolite assemblages are a product of the interaction of a number of factors, including: depth, distance from shore, sediment type, and time.

Eocene lakes were stratified, and that fish, insects, and plants were differentially distributed within them, with deep-water/off-shore environments being dominated by catostomids and other fish, and shallow-water/near-sh ore environments being dominated by amiids, salmonids, percopsoids, and other fish, as well as terrestrial organisms.
